# Datasets in `stelfi` {#sec-data}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
library(stelfi)
library(ggplot2)
```

`stelfi` comes with a number of datasets, listed below. For each one this chapter describes its structure (which is a useful template for preparing your own data) and where it is used in this book. Full details are given in the help files, e.g., `?retweets_niwa`.

```{r}
data(package = "stelfi")$results[, c("Item", "Title")]
```

| Dataset          | Type of data                              | Used in |
|:-----------------|:------------------------------------------|:--------|
| `retweets_niwa`  | Event times                               | @sec-hawkes-applied |
| `uk_serial`      | Summary table (approximate dates)         | -- |
| `multi_hawkes`   | Event times with a stream label (simulated) | -- |
| `nz_earthquakes` | Times, locations, and magnitudes          | @sec-marked-hawkes-applied, @sec-mhawkes-applied, @sec-stelfi-applied, @sec-rtmb |
| `nz_murders`     | Dates and locations                       | -- |
| `sasquatch`      | Dates and locations                       | @sec-sasquatch, @sec-lgcp-gof, @sec-rtmb |
| `iraq_terrorism` | Dates, locations, and event information   | @sec-iraq, @sec-lgcp-iraq-st, @sec-mlgcp-applied |
| `xyt`            | Times and locations (simulated)           | @sec-stelfi-sim |
| `marked`         | Locations with three marks (simulated)    | @sec-mlgcp-sim |
| `horse_mesh`, `horse_sf` | An example mesh and polygon       | @sec-meshmetrics |

## Temporal data

### `retweets_niwa` {.unnumbered}

The times (`POSIXct`, UTC) of the `r length(retweets_niwa)` retweets of NIWA's tweet about a USB stick found in leopard seal scat ([the tweet](https://twitter.com/niwa_nz/status/1092610541401587712)). This is a plain vector of date-times, which needs to be converted to numeric times and sorted before fitting (@sec-hawkes-applied). Retweets are recorded to the nearest second and some share the same second.

```{r}
data(retweets_niwa, package = "stelfi")
head(retweets_niwa)
```

```{r, fig.height = 3, fig.width = 8}
#| message: false
ggplot(data.frame(time = retweets_niwa), aes(x = time)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50) + ylab("Number of retweets") + xlab("") + theme_bw()
```

### `uk_serial` {.unnumbered}

A summary table of `r nrow(uk_serial)` UK serial killers (1828--2015) from [Murder UK](http://www.murderuk.com/), with the approximate number of murders, the years they were active, and (where known) the month and year of the first murder. The dates are approximate (to the month or year), so a Hawkes model would need the times to be jittered within the recorded month or year (@sec-hawkes-data), and with only `r nrow(uk_serial)` events there is little information to estimate self-excitement.

```{r}
data(uk_serial, package = "stelfi")
head(uk_serial)
```

### `multi_hawkes` {.unnumbered}

A simulated two stream Hawkes process with $\mu_1 = \mu_2 = 0.2$, $\beta_1 = \beta_2 = 0.7$, and $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ with diagonal elements 0.5 and off-diagonal elements 0.1 (see @sec-mhawkes). It is a data frame with the sorted event `times` and the `stream` of each event, exactly the format needed by `fit_mhawkes()`.

```{r}
data(multi_hawkes, package = "stelfi")
head(multi_hawkes)
table(multi_hawkes$stream)
```

## Spatial and spatiotemporal data

The following datasets are `sf` objects of type `POINT`, with the location of each event (longitude and latitude) in the `geometry` column and other information in the remaining columns. Before fitting a spatial model the locations should be projected (@sec-lgcp-data). Below, country boundaries for plotting are obtained from the `maps` package.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
boundary <- function(region, database = "world") {
    maps::map(database, region, fill = TRUE, plot = FALSE) |>
        sf::st_as_sf() |>
        sf::st_make_valid()
}
```

### `nz_earthquakes` {.unnumbered}

The origin time (UTC, to the nearest minute), magnitude, and depth (km) of `r nrow(nz_earthquakes)` earthquakes of magnitude 3 and above in the Canterbury region of New Zealand, 2010--2014, from [GeoNet](https://quakesearch.geonet.org.nz/). The period includes the 2010 Darfield and 2011 Christchurch earthquakes and their aftershocks. Some earthquakes share the same recorded minute.

```{r}
data(nz_earthquakes, package = "stelfi")
nz_earthquakes
```

```{r, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 9}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
patchwork::wrap_plots(
    ggplot(nz_earthquakes, aes(x = origintime)) + geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
        ylab("Number of earthquakes") + xlab("") + theme_bw(),
    ggplot(nz_earthquakes) + geom_sf(aes(size = magnitude), alpha = 0.2) + theme_bw(),
    nrow = 1)
```

### `nz_murders` {.unnumbered}

`r nrow(nz_murders)` recorded murders in New Zealand, 2004--2019, from [The Homicide Report](https://interactives.stuff.co.nz/2019/the-homicide-report/), with information on the victim, the cause of death and the region. Dates are recorded to the day, and locations are approximate.

```{r}
data(nz_murders, package = "stelfi")
nz_murders
```

```{r, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 9}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
patchwork::wrap_plots(
    ggplot(nz_murders, aes(x = full_date)) + geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
        ylab("Number of murders") + xlab("") + theme_bw(),
    ggplot(nz_murders) + geom_sf(data = boundary("nz", "nz"), fill = NA) +
        geom_sf(alpha = 0.3) + theme_bw() + coord_sf(xlim = c(165, 180)),
    nrow = 1)
```

### `sasquatch` {.unnumbered}

`r nrow(sasquatch)` reported sasquatch (bigfoot) sightings in the contiguous USA, 2000--2005, collated by the [Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization](https://www.bfro.net/) ([source](https://data.world/timothyrenner/bfro-sightings-data)), with the date and a range of descriptive and weather information. Note that these are *reported* sightings, so their distribution reflects where people are as well as (possibly) where sasquatch are (@sec-lgcp-data). Some sightings share the same location.

```{r}
data(sasquatch, package = "stelfi")
sasquatch[, c("date", "state", "classification")]
```

```{r, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 8}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot(sasquatch) + geom_sf(data = boundary("usa", "usa"), fill = NA) +
    geom_sf(alpha = 0.3) + theme_bw()
```

### `iraq_terrorism` {.unnumbered}

`r nrow(iraq_terrorism)` terrorism events carried out by ISIL in Iraq, 2013--2017, from the [Global Terrorism Database](https://www.start.umd.edu/gtd/). The date is recorded as separate year (`iyear`), month (`imonth`) and day (`iday`) columns, and there is information on each event including the number killed (`nkill`, missing for some events), the spatial accuracy of the recorded location (`specificity`), and the (scaled) population density, luminosity and travel time to the nearest city at the event location.

```{r}
data(iraq_terrorism, package = "stelfi")
iraq_terrorism[, c("iyear", "imonth", "iday", "nkill", "specificity", "popdensity")]
```

```{r, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 9}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
iraq_terrorism$date <- as.Date(paste(iraq_terrorism$iyear, iraq_terrorism$imonth,
                                     iraq_terrorism$iday, sep = "-"))
patchwork::wrap_plots(
    ggplot(iraq_terrorism, aes(x = date)) + geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
        ylab("Number of attacks") + xlab("") + theme_bw(),
    ggplot(iraq_terrorism) + geom_sf(data = boundary("Iraq"), fill = NA) +
        geom_sf(alpha = 0.3) + theme_bw(),
    nrow = 1)
```

## Simulated data

### `xyt` {.unnumbered}

A simulated self-exciting spatiotemporal point pattern of `r xyt$n` events, stored as a `stppp` object (from the `stpp` package): the locations are `xyt$x` and `xyt$y`, the times are `xyt$t` (in $[0, 2]$), and the study region is `xyt$window` (a `spatstat` `owin`, which can be converted to `sf` using `sf::st_as_sf(xyt$window)`). Its study region is used in @sec-stelfi-sim.

```{r, fig.height = 3, fig.width = 8}
data(xyt, package = "stelfi")
ggplot(data.frame(x = xyt$x, y = xyt$y, t = xyt$t), aes(x = x, y = y, size = t)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_sf(data = sf::st_as_sf(xyt$window), fill = NA, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    theme_void()
```

### `marked` {.unnumbered}

A simulated marked point pattern of `r nrow(marked)` events in the square $[0, 3] \times [0, 3]$: a data frame with the locations (`x`, `y`) and three marks, `m1` (Gaussian), `m2` (binary, 0/1) and `m3` (gamma). It is used in @sec-mlgcp-sim.

```{r}
data(marked, package = "stelfi")
head(marked)
```

### `horse_mesh` and `horse_sf` {.unnumbered}

An example mesh (created using `fmesher::fm_mesh_2d()`) and the `sf` polygon it is based on, in the shape of a horse. These are used to illustrate `meshmetrics()` (@sec-meshmetrics) and `get_weights()`.

```{r, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 5}
data(horse_mesh, package = "stelfi")
data(horse_sf, package = "stelfi")
ggplot() + geom_sf(data = mesh_2_sf(horse_mesh), fill = NA) +
    geom_sf(data = horse_sf, fill = NA, col = "red", linewidth = 1) + theme_void()
```
